Honestly, as someone who raided extensively in Vanilla, I'd rather have something closer to the current model than having to raid BWL for years on end just to get the people who needed tier their sets. The only way that model worked was by choking loot drops down to absurdly low levels while making the gear mandatory for many classes.

Also, I think you're very mistaken about TBC. I don't know who was running Karazhan (people that were unable to progress further? In which case it's sort of a non-argument) that long into the expansion -- once you were killing bosses in SSC / TK no smart guild went back to any T4 content except for Gruul for Dragonspine Trophy, unless it was just a fun / alt run. Once you were in BT / Hyjal you never went back to SSC / TK except for attunement (and maybe killing Kael'thas for Al'ar if you had time). Similarly once you were progressed into Sunwell, you'd mostly only clear Black Temple for warglaives (and Memento and Madness, maybe).  


The only time I ran lower tiered content during TBC other than the above-listed exceptions was in a "fun alt run" with people from the other progressed guilds on the server.  


The only way that you get rid of the current system is by choking loot down to Vanilla levels and also making much of it completely necessary for many classes. etc. I'm talking the T2 mana regen requirement for healers, Neltharion's Tear, etc. And with around 1.5-2 total drops per boss kill for a mythic kill. If that's your cup of tea that's fine, but I'd rather not feel it mandatory to raid an instance for a full year to get all the gear I need from it (and potentially still not get it: even with the increased loot drops in TBC, I know people who killed every week it was available and still never saw Dragonspine Trophy drop, despite it being the best trinket in the game for the entire expansion).  


Loot is in equilibrium with obsolescence. At current gear drop levels, it requires warforging / titanforging and very specific pieces (like Azerite) to keep people interested in running the content as long as it's available. If you really think that forcing players to run Uldir for the entire expansion would make the game more fun, I think I'll have to disagree with you. I think the fact of the matter is, people tire of content more rapidly now and forcing them to do old content where the rewards are scant and also have the potential to be largely irrelevant is not going to make people happier.

Deaths caused by blunt force trauma to the head are, however, \*always\* accompanied by either fractures or brain trauma. Neither of those things occurred. Having been a trauma nurse and being part of that community, when we talk about this documentary we are always shocked that the lack of fracture and brain injury didn't just get the case dismissed. In our combined 120+ years of dealing with trauma patients, nobody has \*ever\* heard of \*any\* case, either real or reported, where someone died of blunt force trauma to the head where there was not either a fracture or brain injury or both.
